properties.name: Lab-style viewer
properties.expression: The browser presents the N-Player Go Lab experience against server state: board with Wall coordinates, territory squares, last-move and next-move markers; Home/Back/Forward/End by buttons and keys, and up/down (buttons and arrow keys) choosing among the next moves A, B, ... when a position has two or more, which Forward then follows, or else switching to the previous or next sibling variation; a variation tree and next-move chips; a Search panel listing the viewed position's candidates (visit share and reward) with a heat overlay; per-seat Territory, Bowl, Score, Proj. and Outlook and team totals; a clickable projected-score timeline; GIF export of the viewed line; stone, capture and final-ten-seconds sounds with a toggle; a translucent stone in the mover's colour follows the pointer over every point where a click would place a stone (the viewer's own live turn, or a variation where analysis is open to them) and nowhere else; player colours appear as stones on a wood tile so Black and White are never confused on the dark page; an always-visible play bar (whose turn, clock, Pass, Resign, autopilot) sits above tabs for Scores, Search, Seats and Chat and GIF, where Chat shows unread messages and Seats shows a merge awaiting the viewer's answer; it follows live moves while the viewer is at the latest move and otherwise shows that new moves arrived
properties.formula: AG atom("The browser presents the N-Player Go Lab experience against server state: board with Wall coordinates, territory squares, last-move and next-move markers; Home/Back/Forward/End by buttons and keys, and up/down (buttons and arrow keys) choosing among the next moves A, B, ... when a position has two or more, which Forward then follows, or else switching to the previous or next sibling variation; a variation tree and next-move chips; a Search panel listing the viewed position's candidates (visit share and reward) with a heat overlay; per-seat Territory, Bowl, Score, Proj. and Outlook and team totals; a clickable projected-score timeline; GIF export of the viewed line; stone, capture and final-ten-seconds sounds with a toggle; a translucent stone in the mover's colour follows the pointer over every point where a click would place a stone (the viewer's own live turn, or a variation where analysis is open to them) and nowhere else; player colours appear as stones on a wood tile so Black and White are never confused on the dark page; an always-visible play bar (whose turn, clock, Pass, Resign, autopilot) sits above tabs for Scores, Search, Seats and Chat and GIF, where Chat shows unread messages and Seats shows a merge awaiting the viewer's answer; it follows live moves while the viewer is at the latest move and otherwise shows that new moves arrived")

properties.name: session type panel
properties.expression: Every game tab has a panel, closed until the viewer opens it, that shows the session type of GoServer: the sequence diagram LeanFM draws from the session-type regions of spec/Session.lean, the text it was drawn from, and the question, source, reducer, unit and boundary of the picture; nothing loads until the panel is first opened

properties.expression: Variations made during play and every local Monte Carlo search run in the viewer's browser on a copy of the position, are never sent to the server, never change the game, and are lost when the page closes; after the finish, variation moves become the shared review tree; watchers may branch and search at any time; seated people may browse the actual moves during play and may branch and search once the game has finished; wherever analysis is open, a click on a point, a pass (the P key or the Pass button) or the computer's choice (the C key) plays for whichever seat is to move in the viewed position, as a variation

tasks.title: See the ranking of claimed names and bots

states.label: Server checks identity, scope and bounds

properties.name: ranking is computed from rated games
properties.expression: A game is rated when it finishes with seats on at least two different teams held by rated players; a rated player is a bot (identified by its search settings) or a person whose name was claimed before the game started and whose seat never ran on autopilot; teams are placed by whether a member has not resigned, then team score, ties sharing a place; every two rated seats on different teams make one comparison (a win, a loss or, when tied, half of each) weighted 1/(|A|*|B|) for team sizes |A| and |B| counted in rated seats; ratings are the Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood fit over all comparisons plus one win and one loss for every player against a fixed anchor of 1500, on the Elo scale (400 points per factor of 10); the result is independent of the order games finished; RankingListed orders claimed names and bots by rating and gives each one's rated games and first places

tasks.title: A server bot plays one turn

states.label: Turn starts for a bot-controlled seat
Bot searches with a time budget
Result checked against game, seat and turn revision
Move and its search summary published
Turn ended when the seat's clock ran out

properties.name: bots spend time where it matters
properties.expression: A bot plans each move from its own clock: in main time a share of the remaining main time by the moves it still expects to play, and in byo-yomi part of one period; it stops early once the second-best candidate could not overtake the best in the time it has left, at the planned time unless the top two candidates are close, and never later than the end of the main time plus most of one period, so it never uses up a period on purpose; a move with only one candidate takes no search time; each summary says how long was planned and why the search stopped (settled, planned, close call stretched to the limit, or node cap)
properties.formula: AG atom("A bot plans each move from its own clock: in main time a share of the remaining main time by the moves it still expects to play, and in byo-yomi part of one period; it stops early once the second-best candidate could not overtake the best in the time it has left, at the planned time unless the top two candidates are close, and never later than the end of the main time plus most of one period, so it never uses up a period on purpose; a move with only one candidate takes no search time; each summary says how long was planned and why the search stopped (settled, planned, close call stretched to the limit, or node cap)")

properties.name: bot results are bound to their turn
properties.expression: A bot result changes the game only for the game, seat and turn revision it was dispatched for and only before the seat's clock runs out; the published move carries its search summary: playouts, milliseconds, the time the bot planned for the move and why it stopped, the top candidates with visit counts, the mover's expected reward and every seat's projected final score and outlook, and whether the move replaced a pass to clean up dead stones
properties.formula: AG atom("A bot result changes the game only for the game, seat and turn revision it was dispatched for and only before the seat's clock runs out; the published move carries its search summary: playouts, milliseconds, the time the bot planned for the move and why it stopped, the top candidates with visit counts, the mover's expected reward and every seat's projected final score and outlook, and whether the move replaced a pass to clean up dead stones")
